From b49991d83bba4ae77a560c5f021932e8290bd022 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2024 13:06:39 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: ath12k: fix build vs old compiler
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

gcc 11.4.1-3 warns about memcpy() with overlapping pointers:

drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c: In function ‘ath12k_wow_convert_8023_to_80211.constprop’:
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:114:33: error: ‘__builtin_memcpy’ accessing 18446744073709551611 or more bytes at offsets 0 and 0 overlaps 9223372036854775799 bytes at offset -9223372036854775804 [-Werror=restrict]
  114 | #define __underlying_memcpy     __builtin_memcpy
      |                                 ^
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:637:9: note: in expansion of macro ‘__underlying_memcpy’
  637 |         __underlying_##op(p, q, __fortify_size);                        \
      |         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:682:26: note: in expansion of macro ‘__fortify_memcpy_chk’
  682 | #define memcpy(p, q, s)  __fortify_memcpy_chk(p, q, s,                  \
      |                          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c:190:25: note: in expansion of macro ‘memcpy’
  190 |                         memcpy(pat, eth_pat, eth_pat_len);
      |                         ^~~~~~
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:114:33: error: ‘__builtin_memcpy’ accessing 18446744073709551605 or more bytes at offsets 0 and 0 overlaps 9223372036854775787 bytes at offset -9223372036854775798 [-Werror=restrict]
  114 | #define __underlying_memcpy     __builtin_memcpy
      |                                 ^
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:637:9: note: in expansion of macro ‘__underlying_memcpy’
  637 |         __underlying_##op(p, q, __fortify_size);                        \
      |         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
./include/linux/fortify-string.h:682:26: note: in expansion of macro ‘__fortify_memcpy_chk’
  682 | #define memcpy(p, q, s)  __fortify_memcpy_chk(p, q, s,                  \
      |                          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c:232:25: note: in expansion of macro ‘memcpy’
  232 |                         memcpy(pat, eth_pat, eth_pat_len);
      |                         ^~~~~~

The sum of size_t operands can overflow SIZE_MAX, triggering the
warning.
Address the issue using the suitable helper.

Fixes: 4a3c212eee0e ("wifi: ath12k: add basic WoW functionalities")
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Jeff Johnson <quic_jjohnson@quicinc.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/3175f87d7227e395b330fd88fb840c1645084ea7.1721127979.git.pabeni@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c
index c5cba825a84a..bead19db2c9a 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c
@@ -186,7 +186,7 @@ ath12k_wow_convert_8023_to_80211(struct ath12k *ar,
 	if (eth_pkt_ofs < ETH_ALEN) {
 		pkt_ofs = eth_pkt_ofs + a1_ofs;
 
-		if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < ETH_ALEN) {
+		if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < ETH_ALEN) {
 			memcpy(pat, eth_pat, eth_pat_len);
 			memcpy(bytemask, eth_bytemask, eth_pat_len);
 
@@ -228,7 +228,7 @@ ath12k_wow_convert_8023_to_80211(struct ath12k *ar,
 	} else if (eth_pkt_ofs < prot_ofs) {
 		pkt_ofs = eth_pkt_ofs - ETH_ALEN + a3_ofs;
 
-		if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < prot_ofs) {
+		if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < prot_ofs) {
 			memcpy(pat, eth_pat, eth_pat_len);
 			memcpy(bytemask, eth_bytemask, eth_pat_len);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath12k/wow.c`**
1. **Line 186**: The condition `if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < ETH_ALEN)` was modified to `if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < ETH_ALEN)`.
2. **Line 228**: The condition `if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < prot_ofs)` was modified to `if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < prot_ofs)`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `wow.c` address a compiler warning related to the potential overflow of size calculations when using the `memcpy` function. By replacing the direct addition of `eth_pkt_ofs` and `eth_pat_len` with the `size_add` helper function, the patch ensures that the calculations are safe and do not lead to undefined behavior due to overflow. This change is crucial for maintaining compatibility with older compilers that enforce stricter checks on memory operations. The modifications are directly related to fixing the build issue caused by overlapping pointers in the `memcpy` calls, as indicated by the compiler warnings.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < ETH_ALEN) {
```
```c
if (eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len < prot_ofs) {
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the expressions `eth_pkt_ofs + eth_pat_len` can overflow the maximum value representable by `size_t`, leading to incorrect memory access in the `memcpy` function. This results in warnings about overlapping pointers, as the compiler detects that the calculated sizes may exceed the bounds of the memory being accessed.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < ETH_ALEN) {
```
```c
if (size_add(eth_pkt_ofs, eth_pat_len) < prot_ofs) {
```
Reason:
The patch replaces the direct addition of `eth_pkt_ofs` and `eth_pat_len` with the `size_add` helper function, which safely checks for overflow before performing the addition. This ensures that the calculations do not exceed `SIZE_MAX`, preventing the potential for undefined behavior and addressing the compiler warnings about overlapping pointers.
